0.title: Scope and terminology
0.text: **Tuition total** is the assessed tuition for a student and academic term, before or after adjustments as recorded by the tuition system. **Outstanding balance** is the unpaid amount currently recorded for that student. **Term** identifies the academic billing period (for example, `2026-FALL` or `2027-SPRING`). **Payment confirmation** means the student explicitly approves the amount and term before the assistant submits a payment.

1.title: Payment deadlines > Fall term
1.text: The payment deadline for the Fall 2026 term is **September 30, 2026**. A student should settle the outstanding balance or have an approved installment arrangement by that date.

2.title: Payment deadlines > Spring term
2.text: The payment deadline for the Spring 2027 term is **February 15, 2027**. Deadlines apply in the university's local time zone.

3.title: Payment deadlines > Payment posting
3.text: Payments recorded through supported banking channels may take up to **two business days** to appear in the university account. Students should check their current balance through the Tuition Query API rather than assume a payment has already posted.

4.title: Installment policy > Eligibility
4.text: Students with an outstanding balance of at least **$300** may request an installment arrangement. An arrangement is subject to approval; this policy does not establish whether a particular student has been approved.

5.title: Installment policy > Number and size of installments
5.text: An approved balance may be divided into **up to three installments**. Installments should be equal where possible; any rounding difference is added to the final installment. For example, a $3,000 balance can be divided into three payments of $1,000.

6.title: Installment policy > Installment schedule
6.text: For Fall 2026, approved installment due dates are **September 30, October 31, and November 30, 2026**. For Spring 2027, approved installment due dates are **February 15, March 15, and April 15, 2027**.

7.title: Installment policy > Partial payments versus installment approval
7.text: The payment API can record a partial payment and retain the remaining balance. **A partial payment is not, by itself, approval of an installment plan.** The AI assistant must not promise approval based solely on the policy document or a balance lookup.

8.title: Late fees > Late fee rule
8.text: A **2% one-time late fee** may be assessed on an overdue amount after the applicable due date, unless an approved exception applies. This document describes the rule but does not calculate or post fees automatically.

9.title: Late fees > Example
9.text: If $1,000 is overdue and no exception applies, the illustrative late fee is $20. Whether a fee has actually been posted must be checked in the tuition system.

10.title: Late fees > Exceptions
10.text: Students with a documented university-approved deferral may be exempt. Approval status is not available from this document.

11.title: Scholarships and adjustments > Merit scholarship
11.text: The standard merit scholarship may reduce assessed tuition by **25%** for eligible students. Eligibility is decided by the university and recorded separately.

12.title: Scholarships and adjustments > Scholarship balance questions
12.text: The assistant may explain the 25% rule using this document, but must use the Tuition Query API to report the student's actual tuition total and balance. It must not infer that a student has a scholarship without an authoritative record.

13.title: Refunds and withdrawals > Early withdrawal
13.text: A student who formally withdraws within **14 calendar days of the term start** may be eligible for a refund of **80% of tuition payments associated with that term**, subject to administrative review.

14.title: Refunds and withdrawals > Later withdrawal
14.text: After the 14-day period, refunds are reviewed individually and are not guaranteed. The AI assistant should direct students to the university finance office for a formal decision.

15.title: Refunds and withdrawals > Refund processing
15.text: Approved refunds are generally processed within **15 business days**. This document does not provide refund status for any individual student.

16.title: Banking and payment instructions > Supported workflow
16.text: Students can review tuition information through the university mobile app or a participating banking app. The banking app may query tuition and submit a payment record through the university's Pay Tuition API.

17.title: Banking and payment instructions > Required payment information
17.text: The payment request must identify the **student number, term, and amount**. The payment amount must be positive and must not exceed the current outstanding balance unless the implementation explicitly supports overpayments.

18.title: Banking and payment instructions > Confirmation and safety
18.text: Before initiating a payment, the AI assistant must display the student, term, amount, and current balance, then obtain explicit confirmation. A question such as “Can I pay $500?” is not authorization to submit a transaction.

19.title: Banking and payment instructions > Duplicate submissions
19.text: The payment integration should use an idempotency key or equivalent mechanism to prevent duplicate payment records on retries. The assistant must not claim a payment succeeded until the API returns success.

20.title: Frequently asked questions > When is the Fall tuition deadline?

21.title: Frequently asked questions > Can I pay my balance in three installments?
21.text: The policy permits up to three installments for eligible balances, subject to approval. Check the live balance through the Tuition Query API and see Sections 3.1–3.4.

22.title: Frequently asked questions > Why does my balance still show a payment I made today?
22.text: Payment posting can take up to two business days. See Section 2.3. The live account status must come from the Tuition Query API.

23.title: Frequently asked questions > Can the assistant pay my tuition automatically?
23.text: No. The assistant must obtain explicit confirmation before calling the payment API. See Section 7.3.
